newsitem.title: USA: Washington Mutual to be mortgage giant.
newsitem.headline: Washington Mutual to be mortgage giant.

text.p: Washington Mutual Inc, victorious in the three-month battle to acquire California thrift Great Western Financial Corp, is on the way to becoming a powerhouse in mortgage finance, analysts said.

"Washington Mutual has now emerged as really the dominant player in the mortgage business outside of Fannie Mae amd Freddie Mac," said Jonathan Gray, analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein Co. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the Federal Home Loan Corp, are government-sponsored enterprises which buy mortages from lenders and sell securites backed by the mortgages.

Gray estimated the combined Washington Mutual and Great Western will have a mortgage portfolio of about $80 to $85 billion. That compares to a portfolio valued at close to $300 billion for Fannie Mae.
In a telephone interview, Kerry Killinger, chairman and chief executive of Washington Mutual, said the two companies combined would have just under $90 billion in assets.
He said non-mortgage products such as amd commercial loans are among the faster growing areas in the company.

Washington Mutual appeared the certain winner of Great Western after the only rival bidder, H.F. Ahmanson and Co, dropped out following an adverse court ruling in Delaware. Ahmanson said it was unwilling to raise its bid.
Both Washington Mutual and Great Western have shareholder meetings set for June 13 at which the stock merger must be approved.
The Office of thrift supervision (OTS) must also approve the merger.
"We're highly confident that the regulators will approve this in a timely manner," Killinger said.
He said the companies would continue communicating to shareholders urging a postive vote for the merger.

Killinger said he thought a key event in the three-month saga was a meeting Washington Mutual hosted for investors and analysts in mid-May when it went over its proposal in detail, showed off its management team and its systems technology.

Asked how he viewed the state of Florida, which Washington Mutual will enter for the first time by virtue of the acquisition, Killinger said "We would look for opportunities to grow further both with internal growth and a broader range of consumer products, and potential acquisitions."

He said while Washington Mutual would be spending some time on the integration of Great Western, he expected banking and thrift consolidation to continue in the U.S. and Washington Mutual would continue to take part as an acquirer.

Asked if Washington Mutual's huge presence in mortgages posed any dangers, Gray said there is a lack of diversification of risk but also "a certain advantage to being focused in a narrow field." He noted Washigton Mutual will have a bigger mortgage portfolio than BankAmerica Corp, NationsBank Corp, or Chase Manhattan Corp, which are all larger companies.
Gray said interest rate risk is minimized through use of adjustable mortgages and Washington Mutual has a good record in credit risk.

He said the U.S. mortgage business, with $4 trillion in mortgages outstanding, is bigger than corporate bonds, consumer loans and bank business laons combined. The morgage business is growing at a seven percent annual rate, Gray said.
